source.publication: Fortune / fund filings (BCRED, BlackRock HPS, Ares Strategic Income)

description: A private-credit / semi-liquid alternatives redemption crisis has crystallized since late 2025 and remains ongoing into mid-2026. The listed alternative-asset managers have de-rated sharply from their 2025 peaks — Blackstone ~-46%, Apollo ~-41%, Ares/KKR ~-48%, Blue Owl ~-66% — erasing roughly $265B of market cap. The trigger stack: the Tricolor and First Brands collapses exposed credit-underwriting and mark-to-model concerns, and semi-liquid perpetual vehicles hit redemption gates (Blackstone's BCRED ~$3.8B redemption requests; BlackRock's HPS ~$1.2B / ~9.3% of NAV; Ares Strategic Income ~11.6% of an $22B fund), forcing GPs to fund redemptions from their own balance sheets (Blackstone committed ~$400M to BCRED). Distributions-to-NAV across private-equity funds sit below ~15% for a fourth consecutive year (a record low), and leveraged-loan / IG spreads have widened, freezing the exit and refinancing pipeline. This directly CONTRADICTS the prior bullish thesis for private_equity_listed and the alternatives-fee engine of asset_management (carry crystallization on an M&A/exit reopening) — the 'exit dam breaking' narrative broke the other way. Higher-for-longer rates (cat_20260617_fed_hawkish_pivot) are the macro amplifier: they re-widen LBO financing costs and depress carry NPV. Recorded as a bearish/regime headwind: it is deliberately non-boosting to catalyst_alignment (a sector whose dominant catalyst is a headwind should not be lifted in the heatmap), but it registers the driver, dates it, and lets the regime/exit logic and the review pick it up.

Re-check redemption-gate and spread data at each review; downgrade to decayed only once gates lift and distributions-to-NAV normalize.
